issues.description: Crash in weighted-select: The base case (if (null? options) ...) attempts to call last-pair on options, which is null. This will trigger a runtime error. It should handle the empty list case or return the last valid element.

Broken Replay Interpreter: The replay interpreter delegates output commands to a new instance of make-prompt-interpreter for every instruction. Since each new instance has its own local state which is immediately discarded, the actual output is never captured in the replay's state. run-persona-with-choices will always return an empty string.
Inefficient Execution: Allocating a new interpreter and state object for every single DSL instruction during replay is highly inefficient and creates unnecessary GC pressure.
maybe-emit Limitations: Unlike emit-line, maybe-emit only accepts a single string rather than a variable number of parts, limiting its flexibility for complex dynamic content.

files_reviewed.notes: Critical bugs in weighted-select (null pointer crash) and replay interpreter (broken output capture). Core DSL functions work but edge cases are not handled.

issues.description: Style Inconsistency: Manual use of (emit-line 'bullet ...') immediately follows an emit-list call. It would be cleaner to include this item in the sentinel-critique-triggers list or use a separate emit-list for consistency.

files_reviewed.notes: Well-structured persona definition with good use of the DSL. Only minor style inconsistency found.

issues.description: Stale DSL Primitives: Documentation refers to choice, choose-n, and load-fragment, but the actual implementation in persona-dsl.ss uses pick, pick-n, and try-load-fragment. This will cause confusion.
Incorrect Filename: Refers to agents/lib/persona-prompt-gen.ss, but the actual file is agents/lib/persona-dsl.ss.
Outdated Model Reference: Mentions gemini-3, which may be a placeholder or outdated reference compared to Gemini 2.0 Flash mentioned elsewhere.

files_reviewed.notes: Comprehensive documentation but contains outdated function names and file references that don't match the current implementation.

issues.description: Temp File Leak: fs.unlinkSync(promptFile) is only called inside the successful try path. If execSync fails, the temporary prompt file remains in /tmp indefinitely. It should be unlinked in a finally block.
Missing Validation: No validation that triggerData.author or triggerData.body exist before use. While parseTrigger might handle some errors, a local check is safer.
Predictable Filename: Using Date.now() for a filename in a world-writable /tmp directory is a minor security anti-pattern (predictability). fs.mkdtempSync is preferred.

files_reviewed.notes: Functional script with good structure but needs improved error handling for temp file cleanup and input validation.

issues.description: Score Parsing Bug: (cdr scores) returns a list (e.g., ('7')), not a string. string->number will fail, crashing the pipeline. It should be (cadr scores).
Stage 2 Data Loss: The score-papers stage returns only the calculated scores. The original paper data (Title, Abstract) is lost to the rest of the pipeline chain.

Stage 4 Critical Failure: Because Stage 2 discarded the data, Stage 4 attempts to call assq-ref on paper (which is now a score list) to find 'title'. This will return #f, resulting in 'Title: #f' in all summaries.

Broken Multi-Pipeline: arxiv-multi-category-pipeline maps over categories but calls (invoke-pipeline arxiv-pipeline) without passing the category cat as a parameter, likely running the default category repeatedly.
Hardcoded Filter Threshold: The filter threshold 12 is hardcoded; if haiku returns non-numeric strings, the string->number logic will cause the filter to discard everything.

files_reviewed.notes: Critical data flow bugs make this pipeline non-functional. Score parsing is broken, original paper data is lost between stages, and the multi-category variant doesn't pass parameters correctly.

summary: Gemini Flash QA review identified 16 issues across 5 files. Critical bugs found in persona-dsl.ss (null pointer crash in weighted-select, broken replay interpreter) and arxiv.ss (data flow completely broken - original paper data lost between stages, score parsing bug). README.md has outdated function names. invoke-opus.js has temp file leak on error. sentinel-dsl-v2.ss is well-structured with only minor style issues. Priority fixes needed: arxiv.ss data flow (3 high severity), persona-dsl.ss weighted-select and replay interpreter (2 high severity).
